what_worked: Slides 6–7 median-vs-mean pairing and 'Not used' footnotes show rare editorial discipline and analytical maturity.
fix_next: Reconcile MRR vs 30-day revenue field throughout; several category medians and the $0 count diverge from the reference materially.
verdict: Exceptional narrative and framing; systematic MRR-field ambiguity keeps accuracy from matching the rest.
factual_error_detail: Slide 4/6: AI median $446 vs ref $503, Education $2,142 vs $2,435, Marketing $1,586 vs $2,369.50 — likely MRR vs 30-day field. Slide 4: $0 count 197 vs ref 216. Slide 5: top-1% share shown as 48% implying top-10 ≈49.6% but headline says 'ten companies own half' while chart shows 48% at top 1% (10 companies) — actually close but rounds down. Slide 8: B2B/B2C median ratio 5.7x vs ref 2.35x — substantial discrepancy suggesting different field or denominator.

evidence.insight: Slide 6-7 category pairing (crowding vs payoff) is genuinely original; slide 8 'AI is a layer' reframe and slide 10 correlation hierarchy (subs 0.82 > DR 0.51 > followers 0.16) challenge founder priors with data. Slide 12 acquisition marketplace angle adds non-obvious strategic dimension.
evidence.narrative: Clear power-law thesis from slide 1, built through distribution→concentration→categories→positioning→geography→distribution channels→domains→marketplace→six actionable moves. Every slide has SO WHAT + Not Used footnote. Closing line 'charging is hard' lands the thesis perfectly.
evidence.framing: Slide 3 is exemplary: explains 1,000 rows = top 11% of platform holding 87.6% of revenue, flags self-selection, snapshot limitation, $0-as-null, and missingness per variable group. Audience (founders choosing what to build) is explicit from slide 1.
evidence.accuracy: Directional claims hold but systematic field ambiguity (MRR vs 30-day revenue) creates ~5 discrepancies against reference. Education median off by ~$293, Marketing by ~$784, B2B/B2C ratio 5.7x vs 2.35x is the largest concern. Causal discipline is strong — slide 11 explicitly disclaims causation.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark/light alternation creates rhythm. Dual-axis charts (slides 6, 9, 11) well-labeled. Strong hierarchy: section→headline→subtitle→chart→callouts→SO WHAT→footnote. Donut chart on slide 12 is weakest choice. No decorative filler; every element carries data.
evidence.ai_slop: none — strong editorial voice throughout ('These are assets, not corpses,' specific Not Used justifications, closing aphorism). No generic filler or template language detected.

change_reason: no-change — preliminary scores align with independent assessment across all dimensions. Accuracy at 7.0 correctly reflects systematic field-level discrepancies while acknowledging directional validity and strong causal discipline.
